err.addressPinningWorksInRouter: Address pinning works in Router mode only
err.noAddressIsPinnedFor: No address is pinned for this device
err.saveTheWt32NetworkSettings: Save the WT32 network settings first (password of 8–63 characters)
err.theAddressIsOutsideThe: The address is outside the WT32 network, is the WT32's own, or is pinned to another device
err.theNetworkPasswordMustBe: The network password must be 8–63 characters
err.wt32AddressIpv4EndingIn: WT32 address: IPv4 ending in 1–99 (.100–.200 is the DHCP pool)
page.afterIp: once the device has an IP
page.checkCable: Check that the cable goes into the router and that DHCP is on there. The WT32 looks for DHCP every 30 s.
page.devOtherNet: The device has a static address, {ip}, and no other host of its subnet is on this Wi-Fi network: the device and this page are reachable at that address only from that network. The “{ap}” setup access point stays on, so this page is always reachable through it (http://192.168.4.1). Give the device an address from this network, or DHCP.
page.devReachable: The device is reachable on the network at {ip}.
page.forgetConfirm: Forget the client Wi-Fi network? The WT32 will restart.
page.helpAp: The WT32's cable goes into a router (or a switch of a network with DHCP). The WT32 shares that network over Wi-Fi: addresses, internet and everything else come from the router. This page is at the address the WT32 gets from the router, or http://wt32.local.
page.helpClient: The WT32 joins an existing Wi-Fi. The device on the Ethernet gets its IP from that network's router and is reachable as if it were plugged into it. This page is at http://<device IP>:28480.
page.helpRouter: The WT32 runs its own Wi-Fi and hands out addresses (DHCP), like a router without internet. The device on the Ethernet and the phones share one network and see each other.
page.ipApHint: If there is no DHCP on the cable for 30 s, the WT32 takes this address and hands out .100–.200 to its Wi-Fi clients only, so that this page stays reachable. It goes back to DHCP as soon as DHCP answers.
page.ipOwnHint: The network is the /24 around this address; devices get .100–.200.
page.modeChange: The mode changes after saving and restarting.
page.passLen: The network password must be 8–63 characters
page.pinHint: “Pin”: the device always gets this address, even after the WT32 restarts.
page.relearned: Device forgotten; the WT32 will remember the first one that answers
page.savedAp: Saved. The WT32 restarts with the “{ssid}” network. Connect to it and open http://wt32.local (or the WT32 address in the router's client list); without DHCP on the cable: http://{ip}
page.savedClient: Saved. The WT32 restarts and joins “{ssid}”. Then this page is at http://<device IP>:28480, or through the “WT32-Setup-…” access point while the IP is unknown.
page.savedRouter: Saved. The WT32 restarts with the “{ssid}” network. Connect to it and open http://{ip}
page.setupBoot: One-time setup start (button on the WT32). The saved mode and networks are unchanged: after a restart the WT32 goes back to them unless you save new ones.
page.txWait: Waited for Wi-Fi (its buffers were full)
page.viaSetup: Until the device IP is known, this page is available through the “{ap}” access point.
